name: March Madness
description: NCAA March Madness tournament bracket tracker with round branding, seeded matchups, live scores, and upset highlighting
author: ChuckBuilds

versions.notes: Load the 4x6 detail face on its 7px pixel grid. 4x6-font rasterises cleanly only at whole multiples of 7; at ppem 6 the 1-bit (fontmode "1") mono rasteriser thresholds every glyph down from 4px wide to 3px, so W/M and 0/8 lose the pixels that tell them apart, and getlength returns a fractional advance whose value depends on the installed FreeType -- two boards on one config measured the same string up to 17% apart. Same grid football-scoreboard keeps in _FONT_PIXEL_GRID. PressStart2P is snapped to its own 8px grid in the same pass.

Remove display_options.show_bracket_progress, which was read into an attribute in __init__ and never referenced again -- nothing about bracket progress was ever drawn (#406). Also build the game card's date and time without %-m/%-d/%-I, glibc extensions that raise ValueError on Windows and musl (#414).

versions.changelog: Resolve scroll speed through the shared resolver and apply the frame hold it reports, so slow speeds move whole pixels
Render text 1-bit (no anti-aliasing) so glyphs stay crisp on the LED grid

versions.notes: Final-game layout, and documentation. A finished game drew its date at height - 6 while the 10px score started at height - 13, so the two shared three rows and the date sat inside the score digits -- and because both were offsets from height, they collided at every panel size. The score now lifts clear when a date is coming. Adds real rendered screenshots of the three game states, three of the display toggles and four panel sizes. Marks show_bracket_progress as not implemented: it is read once and never used (#406). Drops three unused imports.

Rebuild the ticker when something else clears its scroll cache. Same defect as odds-ticker: display() decided whether to rebuild by testing its own ticker_image, which Vegas cannot clear when it invalidates the cached scroll image, so the fallback message could be drawn over bracket data the plugin was still holding.

Fix blurry score digits on the LED matrix: the outline-drawing helper used PIL's default anti-aliased text rendering, which blends pixel-font (PressStart2P) glyph edges into dim partial-lit pixels on a 1:1 matrix, muddying numbers (a "6" could read as a "G"). Text now draws in 1-bit font mode so every glyph -- scores, clocks, team names, status text -- renders crisp with no anti-aliasing.

Fix ESPN 403s. Around 2026-08-04 ESPN's site.api began rejecting both browser-style and bare custom User-Agent strings, which returned 403 Forbidden for every request this plugin made. Requests now send an identifying agent with the project URL, which ESPN accepts. No behaviour change beyond the header.

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed.

Add README and LICENSE (GPL-3.0). Conform the manifest to the schema (add required compatible_versions; make dependencies an array). Mount the HTTP retry adapter on http:// as well as https:// so redirected ESPN requests keep the retry/backoff policy.
